clue.text: Give voice about a North European striking

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes round the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a Lapp is a native of Lapland in the far north of Europe

explanation.surface: A singer gets aggressive with a Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like an adjective describing the European, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping is hitting with an open hand, a kind of striking.

clue.text: Most aggrieved, and therefore lie still

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'so I left'
to rest is to lie still

explanation.surface: Someone most upset and so told to lie quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means resentful or upset, so the superlative is most resentful.

clue.text: Transport everyone over the river

indicators.note: over means, in a down entry, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: all means everyone
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Ferrying all passengers across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places ALL above URE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to enrapture or carry them away emotionally, which is to entice and charm.

clue.text: Flap when grabbed by a foreigner — may be drunk

indicators.note: grabbed by means the flap word is held inside the foreigner word

parts.note: a Pole, someone from Poland, is a foreigner to a British setter
a tab is a small flap

explanation.surface: An overseas visitor seizes a flap and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' suggests a tipsy person; here it simply means consumed as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable describes water or liquid fit for drinking.

clue.text: Recess if there's total lack of agreement

parts.note: no means none at all, a total lack
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A break in proceedings when no one can agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner.

clue.text: Start to show to advantage

explanation.surface: Beginning a performance by displaying oneself well.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to begin a journey; to set off a jewel or colour is to enhance it by contrast.

clue.text: Corrupt — and stick up for the lawman!

indicators.note: up means, in a down entry, both pieces together are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: A crooked act and a defence of the police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROTCANE as a whole in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactor is one who enacts, someone who makes laws.

clue.text: A doubter can be quite hard to influence

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sceptic may be very stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unmoved, resisting persuasion.

clue.text: The strong point would appear to be speed

explanation.surface: Speed is the chief advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as fast-ness, the quality of being quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastness is a fortified stronghold; read literally it means quickness.

clue.text: Account for Oriental's agitation

indicators.note: agitation is a stirring up, so the letters of the preceding word are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Explaining why an Eastern person is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' rearranges ORIENTAL; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrative or telling, an account of events.

clue.text: Despicable fellow the underworld finds a worm

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself

explanation.surface: A villain is discovered in hell by something that crawls.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis worm is the larva of the caddis fly, used by anglers as bait.

clue.text: Keeping from cracking jokes?

parts.note: stopping someone telling jokes is silencing them; also, cracking jokes is itself telling gags

explanation.surface: Stopping a comedian from performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagging means silencing someone, and also, in comic slang, telling jokes.

clue.text: A person writing copy in quarters

indicators.note: in places the copying word within the two compass letters

parts.note: the quarters of the compass are its points, here south and east
to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: Someone producing written material while sitting in their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CRIB inside S and E, two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a professional copyist or clerk who writes documents.

clue.text: Shy with press, though not yielding

parts.note: to shy is to throw, or cast
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A bashful person with the media still holds firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron as a figure of speech means rigid and unbending, like the brittle metal.

clue.text: Being surrounded by filth, a large number look disgusted

indicators.note: being surrounded by means the number pieces sit inside the dirt word

parts.note: grime is dirt or filth
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Faced with a lot of dirt, people pull faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being surrounded by' puts A and C inside GRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain.

clue.text: Making fires greater brings the temperature down!

indicators.note: making suggests the following letters are worked into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A paradox: stoking a blaze somehow cools things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' signals that FIRES GREATER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilling food in a fridge lowers its temperature.

clue.text: Note smoker in pub is a musician

indicators.note: in puts the note and smoker inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a drinking room
G is a musical note
a pipe is something smoked

explanation.surface: A man smoking in the local turns out to play an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper is a performer who plays the bagpipes.

clue.text: Virtually of the same standard

explanation.surface: Nearly equal in quality.
explanation.definitionFit: As good as means practically, as in 'as good as finished', and equal in quality to something.

clue.text: Daydreaming, having an inclination to take a holiday?

definitions.text: having an inclination to take a holiday

explanation.surface: A dreamy worker who just wants time off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second part as minded (inclined) to be absent from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent-minded means distracted and inattentive; split up, it means disposed to go missing.

clue.text: They put the squeeze on youngsters

explanation.surface: Bullies pressure children.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers are pincers or claws that pinch; nipper is also British slang for a small child.

clue.text: Out of papers to give out

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: No newspapers left to distribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to utter or put it forth.

clue.text: An artist not all admire — no irony intended

indicators.note: not all means only part of the words admire no irony is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some people genuinely dislike a certain painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across adMIRE NO IRony; the dash is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Withdraw in accordance with new decree

indicators.note: new means the letters of decree are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Retreat in line with a recent edict.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or retreat.

clue.text: Survey the outlook for the future

explanation.surface: Examining what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to explore or search an area; a prospect is an expectation of what is to come.

clue.text: Each one houses a bird

indicators.note: houses means the number word contains the bird inside it

parts.note: an ace is the one on dice or cards
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Every one has a home for a feathered creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie (magpie) is an old crossword favourite for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Stop admitting love for a real swine

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the stopping word takes the love letter inside

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Refusing entry to a lover because he is a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig, literally a swine.

clue.text: Cushioned softly, said little more

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
added means said further, as in 'he added'

explanation.surface: Gently comforting someone, then speaking only a few more words.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded means fitted with soft stuffing to protect or comfort.

clue.text: Remonstrance for having duplicated invitation

indicators.note: duplicated means the invitation word is given twice over

parts.note: come is a word of invitation, as in 'come in'

explanation.surface: A protest at being invited twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Come, come is an exclamation of gentle reproof or protest.

clue.text: Don't give in when sister turns awkward

indicators.note: turns awkward means the word sister is twisted into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Stand firm when a sibling becomes difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand and refuse to yield.

clue.text: Petty cash book to safeguard

parts.note: p, for pence, is small change, the stuff of petty cash
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: An office ledger for small expenses is kept to protect funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a noun after 'Petty cash' but is the verb to reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to keep from harm or decay, to protect.
